guideSights.name: Mary Moto
guideSights.content: Electric bike rental.

guideSights.name: Cappella Sansevero
guideSights.content: A chapel built in 1590, it contains sculptures and other works of art by some of the leading Italian artists of the 18th century, like the extraordinary ''Veiled Christ'' by Giuseppe Sanmartino. It also has a high scientific interest becaus

guideSights.name: San Domenico Maggiore
guideSights.content: One of the most prominent churches of Naples. This Gothic church (est. 1283) incorporates a smaller, original church built on this site in the 10th century, San Michele Arcangelo a Morfisa. The monastery annexed to the church has been the h

guideSights.name: San Gregorio Armeno
guideSights.content: The church was completed in 1640, in honor of Saint Gregory of Armenia and it represents, along with the adjacent monastery, one of the most relevant Baroque complexes in Naples. The interior is decorated with 52 frescoes by Luca Giordano,

guideSights.name: Santa Maria del Carmine Maggiore
guideSights.content: One of Naples' main churches, related to important historical events of the city and its kingdom, such as Masaniello revolt and the executions happened during the five months existence of Parthenopean Republic (1799). The interior is a true

guideSights.name: Castel dell'Ovo
guideSights.content: The oldest castle of the city, located on the former island of ''Megaride'', now a peninsula, on the Gulf of Naples. The castle's name comes from a legend that the Roman poet Virgil (who had a reputation in medieval times as a great sorcere

guideSights.name: Castel Capuano
guideSights.content: The second most ancient castle of Naples after Castel dell'Ovo, built in 12th century by the Normans over a necropolis for use as a royal palace. It was then used as a residence for distinguished visitors such as Francesco Petrarca, and als

guideSights.name: Certosa e Museo di San Martino
guideSights.content: A former monastery complex, now a museum. It is the most visible landmark of the city, perched atop the Vomero hill that commands the gulf. A Carthusian monastery, it was finished and inaugurated under the rule of Queen Joan I in 1368. In 1

guideSights.name: Villa Floridiana and Museo Nazionale della ceramica Duca di Martina
guideSights.content: A large, quiet park with beautiful panoramic views, surrounds a neoclassical villa which hosts a large ceramic collection from different parts of the world.

guideSights.name: Napoli Sotteranea
guideSights.content: Shows former stone quarries, used the city buildings, transformed later to water distribution network, garbage disposal pits and finally a war shelter. You will visit several larger and smaller areas connected by narrow paths - beware if yo

guideSights.name: Neapolis Sotterrata
guideSights.content: Presents ruins of a former Roman market - shops and the like. In addition, entrance to the surrounding museum and chapels is included.

guideSights.name: Napoli sotterranea
guideSights.content: Shows the labyrinth of tunnels, tanks and cavities and takes about 1 hr.

guideSights.name: Galleria Borbonica
guideSights.content: A tour of an old tunnel that connects the palace to military barracks, used as a bomb shelter in World War II.

guideSights.name: Catacombe di San Gennaro
guideSights.content: An extensive, two floor catacombs area restored and maintained by a few dozen local-patriots. Misc. tombs, frescoes, mosaics, etc., are shown.

guideSights.name: Catacombe di San Gaudioso
guideSights.content: A catacombe area where macabre ritual of "draining" was performed. A few remains of skulls in the walls, parts of skeletons and wall paintings are shown. Also the history of the "upstairs" church is shortly showcased.

guideSights.name: Porta Capuana
guideSights.content: Ancient city gate built in 1484, during the Aragonese rule, it represents one of the few visible remains of the medieval walls of Naples. It consists of an arch of white marble decorated with various bas-reliefs, between two impressing cyli

guideSights.name: Fontana del Gigante
guideSights.content: One of the most beautiful fountains of the city, made in the beginning of 17th century by Pietro Bernini, father of the more famous Gian Lorenzo. It was used to sit beside the Royal Palace, close to the statue of a giant. It was then moved

guideSights.name: Fontanelle Cemetery
guideSights.content: These caves in the hillside of Materdei contain a vast ossuary. As of 3/2026 it is still closed for longer renovations. The opening has been delayed for years, so the current prediction of a possible re-opening in 2026 should be taken with

guideSights.name: Royal Palace and National Museum of Capodimonte
guideSights.price: €10 for adult, €2 for EU citizens aged 18-25, €6.50 after 14:00, free with [[Campania#Artecard
guideSights.content: Hosts paintings from the 13th to 18th centuries, including major works by Simone Martini, Raphael, Titian, Caravaggio, Masaccio, Sandro Botticelli, Lorenzo Lotto, Giovanni Bellini, Giorgio Vasari, El Greco, Jacob Philipp Hackert. It also ho

guideSights.name: Museo Civico Filangieri
guideSights.content: Large collection of artworks, coins, and books donated to the city by Prince Gaetano Filangieri.

guideSights.name: Complesso monumentale dei Girolamini
guideSights.price: €5 with reductions, free on first Sunday of the month
guideSights.content: Ecclesiastic complex comprising a gallery of paintings, a cloister, a library of thousands of ancient manuscripts, and a baroque church.

guideSights.name: National railway Museum of Pietrarsa
guideSights.content: A museum housed in the ancient 19th century's Bourbon Factories, along the route of the first railway in Italy: the Napoli-Portici line. Here is possible to admire a large variety of rolling stock like steam locomotives and different period

guideSights.name: Museo Universitario delle Scienze e delle Arti
Albergo dei Poveri
guideSights.content: A former public hospital/almshouse. It was designed by the architect Ferdinando Fuga, and construction was started in 1751. It is five storeys tall and about 300 m long. It was popularly known as "Palazzo Fuga". King Charles III of the Hous

guideSights.name: Palazzo di Sangro di Casacalenda
guideSights.content: 3-stores palace built during the second half of 18th century by the architect Mario Gioffredo. The internal courtyard was designed by Luigi Vanvitelli and features a four-arch portico and Doric order lesenes.

guideSights.name: Underwater Park of Gaiola
guideSights.content: Diving, snorkelling or trip on glass-bottomed boat "Aquavision" in the marine protected area of the minor island of Gaiola, off Posillipo elegant quarter. Just choose your favourite way to discover this stretch of coastline and the surprisi

guideSights.name: Accordi @ Disaccordi - International Short Film Festival
guideSights.content: If you are in Naples during the summer, you can experience the cinema beneath the stars on warm nights, in an amphiteatre equipped with one of the widest projection screens in Italy which rises having an artificial lake all around.

guideSights.name: Di Matteo
guideSights.content: Il presidente, Sorbillo, and his sister, a few doors away (informally known as "la vecchia", the old lady, from the owner of the pizzeria, a very small place with only 4 or 5 tables, that looks like a pizzeria of 50 years ago - very hard to

guideSights.name: Trattoria Don Vincenzo
guideSights.content: Wide choice of dishes in the middle of the old town.

guideSights.name: Decumano 31
guideSights.content: Regional street food in a street with character. Here you can try the Neapolitan frittini.

guideSights.name: 120 Grammi Spaghetti Takeaway
guideSights.content: It's a combination of street food and pasta, with an intense taste: you can choose between a variety of spices.

guideSights.name: Il Cuoppo
guideSights.content: Hole in the wall spot for fried snacks. It's a small eatery for seafood, mozzarella balls, fried zucchini blossoms and anchovies to go.

guideSights.name: L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele
guideSights.content: Pizza Margherita with a crust which is both thin and chewy. There is usually a queue. Get a numbered ticket from the waiter at the door when you arrive, then wait outside for your number to be called. The pizzas are cooked quickly, and they

guideSights.name: Pizzeria Trianon
guideSights.content: The pizzas are less soupy and with crispier crusts.

guideSights.name: Drago d'Oro
guideSights.content: Asian cuisine in a cheap and informal Chinese restaurant close to Via Toledo.

guideSights.name: Trattoria da Peppino Ritrovo degli Artisti
guideSights.content: Simple family restaurant where the owner, Raffaele Liguori, will provide you with local Neapolitan dishes at low prices. Few tables, booking recommended.

guideSights.name: Pizzoteca Quartiere Spagnoli
guideSights.content: Good vibes and pizzas for an affordable price.

guideSights.name: Pizzeria Brandi
guideSights.content: A stone tablet displayed outside the restaurant explains the history of the first pizza margherita, allegedly created here.

guideSights.name: Casetta Rossa di Orsi Francesco
guideSights.content: Known for its good seafood. Also if not very easy to reach it offers one of the best dishes of Mediterranean cuisine.

guideSights.name: Happy Rock Cafe
guideSights.content: Mexican and fusion cuisine in a mid-range pub specialized in fondue.

guideSights.name: Zio Jack Griglieria
guideSights.content: Grill for all the carnivores, near the boardwalk in Santa Lucia.

guideSights.name: Gran Bar Riviera
guideSights.content: Excellent sweet specialties, including ''zeppole'', ''sfogliatelle'' and ''babà''.

guideSights.name: Sfogliatella Mary
guideSights.content: A small pastry shop become a sort of "must-see" for tourists, due to the quality of its Neapolitan pastries, especially the ''sfogliatelle''.

guideSights.name: Gran Caffè Gambrinus
guideSights.content: Enjoy the special Neapolitan coffee in one of the most prestigious and famous cafes in Italy. Founded in 1860 in the rear of Palazzo delle Prefettura, the cafe was also known for being a meeting site for intellectuals, artists and politicia

guideSights.name: Caffè Ciorfito
guideSights.content: Taste the authentic Neapolitan coffee and pastries in a welcoming cafe in the heart of the old town, usually visited by Italian actors.

guideSights.name: Enoteca Belledonne
guideSights.content: Taste the best Italian wines along with cheeses, hams, sausages and pastries in an elegant wine bar and shop in Chiaia district.

guideSights.name: Il Mantegno
guideSights.content: Great wines, cocktails, beer and appetizers in a small but nice wine bar in the historic centre.

guideSights.name: Mosto
guideSights.content: Excellent selection of beer and cocktails in a beautiful pub with jazz music.

guideSights.name: Riva Club
guideSights.content: Seaside disco with an elegant and modern atmosphere, located in front of the island of Nisida.

guideSights.name: Virgilio Club
guideSights.content: Live music and excellent drinks in the enchanting location of Posillipo, overlooking the bay.
